airport: Airports show long, straight runways with distinct markings, connected to large terminal buildings, hangars, and parking structures. They differ from parking lots by having runways and aircraft parking stands rather than vehicle rows; farmland shows crop rows and field boundaries rather than aviation infrastructure; centers lack runways and show dense commercial buildings instead.
bareland: Bare land appears as exposed soil or rock surfaces with minimal vegetation, showing smooth to uneven textures and light brown tones. It contrasts with desert by lacking sand dune formations and being less uniformly sandy; mountain has elevated rocky peaks with shadowed slopes; farmland shows crop rows and organized field patterns rather than bare soil.
baseballfield: Baseball fields show diamond-shaped infields with visible pitcher's mound, baselines, and outfield grass, often with surrounding fences. They differ from stadiums by being open fields without large surrounding stands; parks have irregular wooded areas and paths rather than sports diamonds; playgrounds feature smaller recreational equipment rather than full baseball diamonds.
beach: Beaches appear as sandy or pebbly shorelines along water bodies, with light colors, wave patterns, and occasional beach umbrellas. They contrast with rivers by being coastal or lakeshore rather than inland waterways; desert lacks water adjacency and wave patterns; resorts show buildings and pools alongside beaches rather than natural sand strips.
bridge: Bridges show elevated roadway or railway structures spanning over water or valleys, with visible pillars, deck, and approach ramps. They differ from rivers by being man-made structures crossing over water rather than water channels; viaducts span over land with multiple supports rather than over water; ponds are small water bodies without bridges.
center: Centers are characterized by high-density commercial buildings, large plazas, and major public structures with dense street networks. They contrast with stadiums by having mixed-use towers and offices rather than large sports arenas; churches feature prominent spires and religious architecture rather than commercial blocks; commercial areas have retail signs and parking rather than civic plazas.
church: Churches show distinctive religious architecture with prominent spires, steeples, or domes, often with a central nave and surrounding parking. They differ from centers by being smaller, standalone religious buildings rather than dense commercial blocks; parking lots are open vehicle areas adjacent to buildings; schools show sports fields and classroom wings rather than spires.
commercial: Commercial areas show dense retail and office buildings with large parking lots, wide streets, and visible storefronts or signage. They contrast with centers by having more retail-oriented structures and parking rather than civic and public buildings; industrial zones show large warehouses and smokestacks rather than retail; parking lots lack buildings and serve as vehicle storage.
denseresidential: Dense residential features tightly packed housing units with small yards, narrow streets, and uniform block patterns. It differs from medium residential by having smaller lot sizes and less green space; forest shows dense tree canopy without buildings or roads; sparse residential shows larger lots and more vegetation between houses.
desert: Deserts show vast, barren landscapes with sand dunes, rocky outcrops, and sparse dry vegetation, with uniform light tones. They contrast with bare land by having dune formations and being less disturbed; forests show dense green tree cover rather than sand; beaches are coastal sandy areas adjacent to water.
farmland: Farmland appears as large, open agricultural fields with uniform crop rows, regular field boundaries, and occasional irrigation circles. It differs from meadow by having organized crop rows rather than natural grassland; pond appears as small water bodies within fields; industrial areas show factories and storage rather than crops.
forest: Forests show dense tree canopy with dark green textures, irregular edges, and no visible ground, often covering large areas. They contrast with desert by having dense vegetation rather than sand; mountains have exposed rocky peaks and slopes; dense residential shows buildings and roads instead of tree cover.
industrial: Industrial areas feature large warehouses, factories, smokestacks, and extensive parking lots with regular blocky layouts. They differ from storage tanks by having buildings and smokestacks rather than circular metallic containers; railway stations show tracks and passenger buildings rather than industrial structures; farmland shows agricultural fields rather than factories.
meadow: Meadows show open, grassy areas with smooth, uniform texture, often with scattered trees or shrubs, and no field lines. They contrast with farmland by lacking organized crop rows and field boundaries; pond are small water bodies within meadows; baseball fields have sports markings and infield dirt rather than natural grass.
mediumresidential: Medium residential shows moderately sized houses on medium lots with visible yards, driveways, and tree-lined streets. It differs from dense residential by having larger lots and more green space; sparse residential shows widely spaced houses with large wooded lots; resorts show hotel buildings, pools, and recreational facilities rather than residential neighborhoods.
mountain: Mountains show elevated, rugged terrain with steep slopes, rocky outcrops, and shadow patterns, often with forested lower elevations. They contrast with forests by having exposed rock and elevation changes rather than uniform tree cover; desert shows flat sand dunes rather than rocky peaks; bare land lacks the dramatic elevation and ridges.
park: Parks show green open spaces with trees, walking paths, ponds, and recreational areas, often irregular in shape. They differ from ponds by being larger areas with vegetation and paths rather than just water; squares are paved public plazas without extensive grass; baseball fields are sports-specific with diamond markings.
parking: Parking lots appear as flat, paved areas with rows of vehicles, clear lane markings, and entrance/exit points. They differ from airports by having no runways or aircraft and being smaller in scale; ports show water, docks, and ships rather than vehicle rows; churches have a central building with surrounding parking rather than just open lots.
playground: Playgrounds show recreational areas with equipment like slides, swings, and courts, often within parks or schools. They differ from stadiums by being smaller recreational zones without large stands; schools have multiple buildings and larger campus areas; baseball fields have diamond infields rather than recreational equipment.
pond: Ponds appear as small, circular or irregular water bodies with calm surfaces, often surrounded by vegetation. They contrast with rivers by being still, enclosed water rather than flowing channels; farmland shows crop fields rather than water features; parks are larger green areas with paths and trees rather than just water.
port: Ports show waterfront areas with docks, piers, ships, cranes, and large storage areas adjacent to water. They differ from parking lots by having ships and water rather than vehicles; industrial areas lack the extensive waterfront and docks; beaches show natural sandy shorelines without port infrastructure.
railwaystation: Railway stations show tracks, platforms, passenger buildings, and surrounding parking lots, often with linear rail lines. They contrast with industrial areas by having passenger buildings and platforms rather than factories; parking lots show only vehicle storage without tracks; airports have runways and terminals rather than train tracks.
resort: Resorts show hotel buildings, pools, tennis courts, and landscaped grounds, often near beaches or recreational areas. They differ from beaches by having buildings and pools rather than natural sand; medium residential shows permanent housing rather than resort facilities; parks have natural vegetation and paths rather than hotel and pool complexes.
river: Rivers appear as narrow, sinuous, dark water channels with flowing patterns and riparian vegetation along banks. They contrast with ponds by being elongated flowing water rather than still, enclosed water bodies; bridges are structures spanning across rivers; beaches show sandy shorelines along water rather than water channels themselves.
school: Schools show campus layouts with classroom buildings, playgrounds, sports fields, and surrounding parking lots. They differ from playgrounds by having multiple buildings and larger campus areas; parks show natural vegetation and paths rather than school facilities; parking lots lack buildings and are just open paved areas.
sparseresidential: Sparse residential shows widely separated houses surrounded by large vegetated lots, with unpaved roads and low building density. It contrasts with medium residential by having larger lot sizes and more vegetation between houses; forest shows tree cover without houses; ponds are small water features within residential areas.
square: Squares show paved public plazas with geometric layouts, central monuments or fountains, and surrounding buildings. They differ from parks by being paved with minimal grass and more formal geometry; centers have taller denser buildings around but lack the open plaza space; parking lots show vehicle rows rather than public gathering areas.
stadium: Stadiums show large sports or event venues with oval or rectangular shape, tiered seating, and surrounding parking lots. They contrast with baseball fields by having enclosed stands and larger scale; centers show commercial towers rather than sports venues; playgrounds are much smaller recreational areas without stands.
storagetanks: Storage tanks appear as large circular metallic containers with domed or flat roofs, arranged in industrial clusters. They differ from industrial areas by being rows of tanks rather than factories and smokestacks; ponds are water bodies rather than metallic structures; desert shows sand dunes rather than tank farms.
viaduct: Viaducts show elevated road or rail structures with long continuous sections and multiple supports, often crossing over land. They differ from bridges by spanning over land rather than water; parking lots are ground-level open areas without elevated structures; playgrounds show recreational equipment rather than infrastructure.
